subject: Procurement readiness & pricing/packaging alignment for FinApps
messages:
<headers>
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@finapps.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement readiness & pricing/packaging alignment for FinApps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to help your procurement team move forward:

1) Commercial path options we discussed
   - Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand): no long-term commits, billed to card or corporate billing account. Fastest to go live.
   - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commits for predictable throughput and lower unit costs. Requires PO/billing setup.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise license + support, paper contract, typically longer procurement lead time.

2) Procurement questions you flagged
   - PO vs card: you can start on card for POC and then move to PO with net-30 terms for Dedicated/Private.
   - Marketplace: we are listed on AWS Marketplace (can do consolidated billing) — good if your procurement prefers marketplace purchases.
   - Paper process: we can provide an SOW and standard enterprise agreement. I attached a procurement checklist and pricing workbook for reference.

Next steps
   - I'll loop in our AE (Priyom) and SE (Aditya) to provide a tailored pricing estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for your Q1 workload.
   - Can you share your procurement contact and preferred billing path (PO through AP / procurement portal / card)? Also any template redlines early will help.

If helpful, we can set a 30-min call with procurement and legal next week to walk through paper process and timelines.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_Procurement_Checklist.pdf, Redwood_PRICING_2026.xlsx

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks — noted on Ben as the procurement contact. Short answers here and next steps:

- Marketplace: yes, we are on AWS Marketplace and it supports consolidated billing and marketplace-based PO flow. I'll include a Marketplace purchase option in the pricing workbook.

- PO vs Card: POC on a card is a common pattern. When you decide to move to Dedicated, we can switch to PO with net-30 terms. For Private deployments we typically require a signed enterprise agreement and onboarding timeline.

- Dedicated timelines: typical procurement + SOC2 review + procurement onboarding is ~6–10 weeks (45–75 days) depending on legal review; 60–90 days is a reasonable planning window. We'll provide a checklist to accelerate (what to expect: COLO/networking requirements only if private; for Dedicated most work is around billing and contractual terms).

- Security/compliance evidence: we can provide SOC 2 report, data flow diagrams, and an architecture checklist. Aditya — can you prepare a short security packet and a note on VPC/on-prem pre-reqs for Ben?

Next steps / Actions:
1) Priyom will prepare a pricing comparison (Hosted on-demand vs Dedicated reserveds) and include marketplace pricing and indicative commit tiers.
2) Ben — if you can share the vendor questionnaire, we'll populate and return within 3 business days.
3) Let's tentatively schedule a procurement call the week of Nov 22 — Marissa, Priyom, Aditya, Ben, and Alice. Please share availability.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_Procurement_Checklist.pdf, Redwood_PRICING_2026.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Draft commercial path & pricing outline for FinApps (for call prep)

Marissa / Aditya —

Draft notes for the Nov 22 procurement call. High level:

- POC: Hosted API, card billing. Estimate usage 1.5M tokens/month. Cost: $0.004/token (on-demand) => ~$6k/month. Include optional rate limit for budget control.
- Dedicated: Target baseline commit for Q1: 200 concurrent tokens/sec equivalent — suggest a 12-month commit with a 20% discount vs on-demand unit cost. Include burst capacity pricing.
- Marketplace: Provide listing price and marketplace fees; note potential delay in revenue recognition for marketplace purchases — flag with finance.
- Paper process: Standard EULA + SOW. SOW to include: service levels (SLA), onboarding timeline, data handling, and support scope.

Action items:
- Aditya: bring the security packet (SOC2 excerpt + network checklist) to the call.
- Marissa: confirm availability for Nov 22. I'll draft the pricing slide and include marketplace option.

I'll attach an internal pricing slide in follow-up.

Thanks,
Priyom
